newsitem.title: USA: Compass says to buy Daka for $195 mln. [CORRECTED 14:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Compass says to buy Daka for $195 mln. [CORRECTED 14:15 GMT]

text.p: Compass Group PLC said Wednesday its Compass Holdings Inc unit is in a definitive agreement to buy the contract foodservice business of Daka International for about $195 million.
The company said about $85 million will be paid to the stockholders of Daka International through a cash tender offer of $7.50 per share, and $110 million will be used to repay Daka debt.
Daka stockholders will also receive shares of a new company that will own all of Daka's non-foodservice business.
Compass said the deal will be accomplished by Daka first spinning off its restaurant business to its shareholders, and Compass making a cash tender offer for all the shares of Daka's common stock.
After the tender offer, Compass will merge Daka with one of its subsidiaries.
Compass will not acquire the non-foodservice business of Daka International.
Compass plans to finance the deal with funds from established cash sources.
The Bank of New York is depository in the tender offer and MacKenzie Partners Inc is the information agent.
Compass Group is a foodservice company that employs about 120,000 people worldwide.
Daka International is a foodservice and restaurant company operating in the contract foodservice management industry and the restaurant industry.

Compass president and chief executive Mike Bailey said Allen Maxwell, president and chief operating officer of Daka, will remain president of Daka and will become a member of the Compass Group USA Division board following the acquisition.

"We are truly delighted to have Allen join us," Baily said. "Together we will progress with our stated business strategy of further development in the education market, and continue our efforts in strategic business segmentation."
